key_insight: Fully alloyed WC–Co–Cr powder enables dense, layered coatings, while spray method selection controls the tradeoff between hardness and tribological performance.
engineering_relevance: The study identifies process routes for optimizing wear-resistant WC–Co–Cr coatings on machine parts operating under high friction and load.
method: Compared detonation spraying (DS) and HVOF for WC–Co–Cr cermet coating deposition.
Characterized powder morphology and coating microstructure using SEM and EDS.
Assessed phase/structure quality and tribological behavior, including microhardness and friction coefficient.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports average microhardness of 1449 HV for DS coatings and a low friction coefficient of Kt = 0.143 for HVOF coatings, supporting method-dependent performance differences.
watch_item: Results depend strongly on powder homogeneity and spray parameters, so performance may not transfer directly to other feedstocks or deposition settings.
paper_title: INVESTIGATION OF THE FORMATION OF STRUCTURE AND WEAR-RESISTANT PROPERTIES OF WC–CO–CR COATINGS PRODUCED BY HVOF AND DETONATION SPRAYING
